移.meaning: A farmer stacks <part>many</part> sacks of <part>grain</part> on the left side of his boat, and it tips. He drags them all to the right: it tips the other way. All night long, grunting and sweating, he has to <kanji>shift</kanji> them back and forth.
移.on: An <sound>ee</sound>l in the river watches, giggling every time the boat leans.
移.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>ps,' he says, as a sack splits and the dust makes him sneeze: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

談.meaning: Two dragons meet in a little café, and every word of their <part>speech</part> comes out as a puff of <part>flame</part>. The menu catches fire, then the curtains, then the waiter's hat. They keep chatting politely: they have so much to <kanji>discuss</kanji>.
談.on: Afterwards the owner locks them in a damp <sound>dun</sound>geon to cool off.

倒.meaning: A gang of rebels marches into the palace, hangs their hats on the royal <part>coat hook</part> and sits down on the throne. On the day of their <part>arrival</part>, the old king is out in his slippers buying milk. That's a quick <kanji>overthrow</kanji>.
倒.on: Coming home, the king stubs his <sound>toe</sound> on the locked palace gate.
倒.kun: Then he trips over a dropped <sound>ta</sound>co and falls flat: '<sound>Oh</sound>!'

与.meaning: An old queen turns a golden <part>faucet</part> in the palace wall, and out drips exactly <part>one</part> diamond. Her servants <part>wrap</part> it in silk and carry it to a farmer's daughter. It's a gift only a queen could <kanji>bestow</kanji>.
与.on: The girl sends back a thank-you pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt.
与.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' she gasped when it arrived, dropping her <sound>ta</sound>co in the mud.

八.meaning: Two skiers zoom down a snowy slope side by side, then one swerves left and one swerves right, carving tracks that spread apart like the numeral <part>eight</part>. At the bottom they count their bruises: <kanji>eight</kanji> each.
八.on: '<sound>Ha</sound>, <sound>chee</sound>se!' they shout, as a friend snaps a photo of their tracks.
八.kun: '<sound>Yup</sound>,' nods the instructor, counting them again on his gloves.

検.meaning: A park ranger climbs a <part>tree</part> above the <part>campsite</part> with binoculars and peers into every tent: are the fires out, the bins shut, the marshmallows shared fairly? She writes a score for each. Every camper dreads her <kanji>examination</kanji>.
検.on: Even the dogs' <sound>ken</sound>nel gets a mark out of ten.
検.kun: Peeking from behind a leafy <sound>shi</sound>eld, she cheers '<sound>Rah</sound>!' at the tidiest tent.

歌.meaning: A frog starts croaking on stage and the audience lets out a big <part>yawn</part>. But he keeps going, louder and sweeter, until the judges nod their <part>approval</part> one by one and start swaying. By the end, everyone is humming along to his <kanji>song</kanji>.
歌.on: Even a <sound>ca</sound>rp leaps out of the pond to join the chorus.
歌.kun: Afterwards they all slurp <sound>u</sound>don and munch <sound>ta</sound>cos backstage.

丸.meaning: A baker drops a single <part>dot</part> of dough and kicks it <part>nine</part> times across the kitchen floor. Each kick rolls it bigger and smoother, until it bounces like a ball. Now it's perfectly <kanji>round</kanji>.
丸.on: The floor is coated in sticky <sound>gun</sound>k from all that kicking.
丸.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, look!' The baker's son sets a <sound>ru</sound>by on top like a cherry.

勢.meaning: A tiny <part>gardener</part> drinks a whole watering can of tonic and swells up with <part>muscle</part>. He yanks out a tree stump, flings the shed over the hedge and pushes back a herd of charging goats. He alone is a match for an army's <kanji>forces</kanji>.
勢.on: For his next trick, he lifts the bank's steel <sound>sa</sound>fe over his head.
勢.kun: '<sound>Ea</sound>sy!' squeaks a <sound>ki</sound>wi bird on the fence. '<sound>Oh</sound>, look at him go!'

識.meaning: In a noisy hall, a hundred people give a <part>speech</part> at once while someone bashes a <part>war gong</part>. Only one old owl can pick out each voice: who's lying, who's joking, who's telling the truth. She has a gift: she can <kanji>discern</kanji>.
識.on: <sound>She</sound> locks the liars' notes away with a golden <sound>key</sound>.
識.kun: Then she peeks out from behind her <sound>shi</sound>eld: she knows exactly who did it.

笑.meaning: A man in a <part>tilted hat</part> walks through a grove of <part>bamboo</part>, and the stalks tickle his ears, his nose and his ribs. He tries to stay serious, but his hat slips further and he doubles over. He can't help it: he has to <kanji>laugh</kanji>.
笑.on: It's the funniest <sound>show</sound> in the woods; even the birds buy tickets.
笑.kun: He laughs so hard he drops his <sound>wa</sound>sabi into his <sound>ra</sound>men.

個.meaning: Every guest at the party hangs a coat on one long <part>coat hook</part>, then presses a thumb into soft clay and lets it <part>harden</part> into a little name badge. No two thumbprints are the same. Each badge belongs to one <kanji>individual</kanji>.
個.on: Even the <sound>ko</sound>ala gets its own badge, with a fluffy ear print.

省.meaning: A stingy one-eyed pirate glares with his single bloodshot <part>eye</part> at his candle and lets it burn for only a <part>few</part> seconds a night, then counts his coins in the dark. He even rations his parrot to a few words a week. 'Waste nothing,' he growls. He lives to <kanji>conserve</kanji>.
省.on: He even turns off the lights in the middle of a <sound>show</sound> to save power.
省.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' he snorts, and trims his <sound>bu</sound>shy beard by half: less to wash.

深.meaning: A fisherman ties his <part>net</part> to the top of a tall <part>tree</part> and lowers it into a dark lake, <part>water drops</part> dripping off every branch. Down, down, the whole tree slides in after it and still doesn't touch the bottom. That lake is very <kanji>deep</kanji>.
深.on: He leans over to look and bangs his <sound>shin</sound> on the edge of the jetty.
深.kun: He gives up and floats on a <sound>fu</sound>ton, while a <sound>ca</sound>rp swims down to look for his tree.

構.meaning: A <part>tree</part> wants to look its best for a painter, so it leans on some <part>scaffolding</part>: chest out, branches back, chin up. It holds the pose for nine hours without a wobble. The painter calls it perfect <kanji>posture</kanji>.
構.on: A squirrel on the scaffold licks an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne the whole time.
構.kun: The painter's <sound>ca</sound>lm <sound>ma</sound>ma holds the easel steady and takes her stance beside it.

破.meaning: A caveman stretches a bear <part>pelt</part> over a big <part>stone</part> to make a cosy seat. He pulls one corner, then the other, harder, harder: rrrip! It splits right down the middle. He's managed to <kanji>rend</kanji> it in two.
破.on: Now he has only half a rug for the floor of his <sound>hu</sound>t.
破.kun: He drags the torn halves out into the <sound>ya</sound>rd and hangs them on a <sound>bu</sound>sh.

補.meaning: A farmer's <part>weathervane</part> loses one arm in a storm, so he tapes a <part>flyswatter</part> to the stump. Now it spins again, and swats flies as it turns. It's not the real thing, but it's a handy <kanji>supplement</kanji>.
補.on: A fly lands on the farmer's <sound>ho</sound>tdog, and whap!
補.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' honk the <sound>gee</sound>se, as it swats a fly off their <sound>na</sound>an.

認.meaning: A shy knight has to <part>endure</part> a long <part>speech</part> from a dragon, listing every village it has ever burnt. At the end the dragon sniffs, 'Fine. You did beat me.' The knight finally gets the nod he wanted: the dragon has to <kanji>acknowledge</kanji> him.
認.on: A <sound>nin</sound>ja hidden in the rafters writes it all down as proof.
認.kun: '<sound>Me</sound>?' squeaks the knight, standing on <sound>to</sound>p of the rubble.

等.meaning: At the <part>temple</part> fair, a monk lists everything for sale on a strip of <part>bamboo</part>: brooms, bells, buns, bowls, beads... The list runs out of room, so he scratches three little dots at the end. That means <kanji>etc.</kanji>
等.on: He drops the bamboo strip on his <sound>toe</sound> and adds one more item: bandages.
等.kun: <sound>He</sound> piles buns on <sound>to</sound>p of the scales until both sides match: equal.

草.meaning: A greedy goat sets its alarm clock for <part>early</part> every morning, sneaks into the neighbour's garden and nibbles each tuft of <part>grass</part> before anyone wakes. By breakfast the lawn is bare, but by evening it has all grown back. It's magic <kanji>grass</kanji>.
草.on: The neighbour scrubs the goat's muddy hooves with a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p.
草.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo flies down and <sound>su</sound>cks up a long blade like spaghetti.

提.meaning: A sailor drops his ship's <part>anchor</part> in the harbour, angled <part>just so</part>, right in front of his sweetheart's window. Tied to its chain is a ring. He kneels on deck and shouts up to her: he's come to <kanji>propose</kanji>.
提.on: The ring is stuck to the anchor with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.
提.kun: She leans out in her best silk <sound>sa</sound>ri and lowers a basket on a rope for the ring.

児.meaning: In a museum of <part>old times</part>, an ancient stone doll on a shelf suddenly sprouts two wobbly <part>legs</part>, toddles to the edge and wails for milk. The guards panic and fetch a bottle. It's a <kanji>newborn babe</kanji>.
児.on: They rush it to hospital in a muddy <sound>jee</sound>p.
児.kun: It falls asleep in the back, hugging a toy <sound>ko</sound>ala.

遺.meaning: An old pirate rolls a chest of <part>precious</part> pearls down the <part>ramp</part> of his ship to his parrot. 'When I'm gone, it's all yours.' The parrot squawks and starts writing a will on the deck in feathers. Everything he owns, he will <kanji>bequeath</kanji>.
遺.on: The cat gets just one jar of pickled <sound>ee</sound>l.
遺.kun: '<sound>No</sound>t the <sound>ko</sound>ala,' he adds. 'That one stays behind with me.'

逆.meaning: An <part>uprooted sprout</part> rolls down a <part>ramp</part> head over heels and lands with its leaves in the soil and its roots waving in the air. It likes it that way and grows up the wrong way round, apples at the bottom. It's a tree <kanji>inverted</kanji>.
逆.on: A goat takes one bite of an upside-down apple and spits it out with a bi<sound>g</sound> '<sound>Yuck</sound>!'
逆.kun: The tree's story becomes a long <sound>sa</sound>ga, told by a <sound>ca</sound>rp in the pond below.

柄.meaning: A lodger in a cheap <part>third class</part> cabin is bored, so he carves the wooden <part>tree</part> of a bedpost into swirls, leaves and little owls. Soon every passenger wants a look. The poorest cabin on the ship has the finest <kanji>design</kanji>.
柄.on: His mattress is just a sack of <sound>hay</sound>, but he even carves patterns into that.
柄.kun: A <sound>gu</sound>ll pecks at the swirls through the porthole and caws '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

答.meaning: A class racks its brains over a puzzle box with no key. One girl snaps off a stick of <part>bamboo</part> and whittles it until it slides into the keyhole with a perfect <part>fit</part>. Click: the lid pops. She's found the <kanji>solution</kanji>.
答.on: Inside is a tiny wooden <sound>toe</sound>, which makes no sense at all.
答.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala in the back row shouts the answer through a mouthful of <sound>ta</sound>co.

型.meaning: To <part>punish</part> a cheeky gnome, the garden queen presses him face first into wet <part>soil</part>. When he climbs out, a perfect gnome-shaped hole is left behind. She fills it with plaster and makes a hundred copies from the <kanji>mould</kanji>.
型.on: She also uses it to bake a gnome-shaped <sound>ca</sound>ke.
型.kun: Every copy wears the same <sound>ca</sound>lm smile and holds the same <sound>ta</sound>co.

養.meaning: A <part>sheep</part> finds a dragon egg in the hay, hatches it under her wool and spoons <part>food</part> into its mouth: porridge, peppers, a whole pumpkin. The dragon grows bigger than the barn but still calls her mum. She chose to <kanji>foster</kanji> it.
養.on: To keep it busy she gives it a giant <sound>yo</sound>-yo that rolls slowly down and back up the barn wall.
養.kun: In the <sound>ya</sound>rd she shelters it behind a <sound>shi</sound>eld and feeds it warm <sound>na</sound>an.

乱.meaning: In a quiet library, someone sticks out their <part>tongue</part> at the librarian. She throws a book; it bounces off the shelves in a <part>zigzag</part>, knocks over a ladder, and soon everyone is hurling dictionaries and swinging from the lamps. A full-blown <kanji>riot</kanji>.
乱.on: The noise carries all the way to an airport <sound>run</sound>way, where a plane has to circle.
乱.kun: 'Not <sound>me</sound>!' squeaks the culprit, then jumps up on a table: 'Ta-<sound>da</sound>!'

傷.meaning: A swimmer hangs her towel on the <part>coat hook</part>, climbs the <part>diving board</part> and stares up into the <part>sunbeams</part>, dazzled. She misses the pool and belly-flops onto the tiles. Ouch. One bandage won't cover that <kanji>wound</kanji>.
傷.on: Everyone at the pool claps anyway: it was quite a <sound>show</sound>.
傷.kun: Her mum drops the car <sound>keys</sound> as she runs for the first aid kit.
